header.name: Design for Artificial Intelligence driven Products
header.description:
Designing for AI means designing for a human-machine relationship that is in flux; this contrasts with non-AI design where the relationship is static.

AI-driven products bring together a collection of technologies (machine learning, knowledge representation and reasoning, natural language processing, computer vision, and robotics) to endow machines with increasingly human-like physical, cognitive, and emotional capabilities. AI-driven products can learn from user behavior patterns and personalize the experience of a consumer. The evolution of human-machine interactions from a context where the human adapts to the machine and the machine does not (i.e., traditional human-machine interaction), to a context where the human and the machine learn from and adapt to each other requires conceptualization about the nature of relationships consumers have with AI-driven products.

What does it mean to design for AI? How do you create responsible, ethical, human- centered experiences? AI-driven products need to be engineered (i.e., made to work) but they also need to be designed (i.e., made with purpose.)  As we begin to outsource human decision-making capabilities to machines, it is important to design & create not just functional, but ethical and safe, artificial intelligence.

Based on the intersection of technology (Artificial Intelligence) and design-thinking, the course offers a blend of theoretical insights and practical skills in AI product development, tailored for engineering students with a keen interest in AI, business and design innovation. Explore the future of AI applications in real-world scenarios, and gain hands-on experience to develop real solutions that humans need.

By the end of the course, students would be more familiar with steps to follow for designing for AI. In small groups, they will prepare working protype of artificial intelligence driven products
